structure.overview: WestJet appeals the Canada Industrial Relations Board's decision that found the respondent was unjustly dismissed and that his unwelcome sexual comments did not amount to sexual harassment. The Federal Court of Appeal found the Board's conclusion on sexual harassment unreasonable and contradictory, setting aside the decision and remitting the matter for reconsideration. The court upheld other findings of the Board, including the respondent's mental health challenges and the appropriateness of the adjudicator.

party_points.text: Board's sexual harassment conclusion unreasonable and contradictory
Court should defer to Board's reasoned findings under reasonableness standard and dismiss application

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Supreme Court defines sexual harassment as unwelcome sexual conduct harming the work environment or causing adverse job consequences.

citations.cite: Janzen v. Platy Enterprises Ltd., 1989 CanLII 97 (SCC), [1989] 1 SCR 1252 [Janzen] at p. 1284
citations.why: Definition of sexual harassment by Supreme Court

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Textbooks define sexual harassment broadly, including overt advances, lewd comments, and unwelcome sexual behavior in the workplace.

citations.cite: Donald J.M. Brown, David M. Beatty & Adam J. Beatty, Canadian Labour Arbitration, 5th ed (Toronto: Thompson Reuters Canada, 2019) [Brown & Beatty] at § 7:33
citations.why: Definition of sexual harassment including various forms

citations.cite: Arjun Aggarwal, Sexual Harassment in the Workplace, 2nd ed. (Toronto: Butterworths, 1992) at p. 7
citations.why: Definition of sexual harassment including subtle and obvious behaviors

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Supreme Court states sexual harassment is a demeaning practice attacking employee dignity and self-respect.

citations.cite: Janzen at p. 1284
citations.why: Sexual harassment as affront to dignity and self-respect

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Canada Labour Code defines harassment and violence to include sexual conduct causing offence or injury to employees.

citations.cite: Canada Labour Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. L-2, s. 122(1)
citations.why: Statutory definition of harassment and violence including sexual nature

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Sexual harassment does not require sexual intent or awareness by the harasser, only that comments are sexual and offensive objectively.

citations.cite: Calgary (City) v. Canadian Union of Public Employees Local 37, 2019 ABCA 388 at paras. 36, 43–44
citations.why: Sexual harassment requires objective sexual nature and offensiveness

citations.cite: Laurie and Bell Media, Re (2020), 2020 CarswellNat 5204 (Can.Adjud. (CLC Part III)) at paras. 197–200
citations.why: Sexual harassment requires objective sexual nature and offensiveness

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Lewd or demeaning comments and pornography distribution can constitute sexual harassment even without sexual intent.

citations.cite: Sterling Crane and IUOE, Local 955 (Cormier), Re, 2024 CanLII 46844 (Alta. Arb.) at para. 140
citations.why: Lewd comments can be sexual harassment without sexual intent

citations.cite: Alberta Justice and Solicitor General and AUPE (869395), Re, 2023 CarswellAlta 160, [2023] A.W.L.D. 1215 at para. 79
citations.why: Lewd comments can be sexual harassment without sexual intent

citations.cite: Brown & Beatty at § 7:33
citations.why: Lewd comments can be sexual harassment without sexual intent

citations.cite: Poliquin at paras. 55–60
citations.why: Distribution of pornography is sexual harassment

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: Only WestJet's arguments about the Board's sexual harassment conclusion justify intervention.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board's decision is reviewed on a reasonableness standard and entitled to deference.

citations.cite: Essaï v. Toronto-Dominion Bank, 2024 FCA 65 at paras. 7–9
citations.why: Reasonableness standard applies to Board decision

citations.cite: Northern Inter-Tribal Health Authority Inc. v. Yang, 2023 FCA 47 at paras. 46–48
citations.why: Reasonableness standard applies to Board decision

citations.cite: Amer v. Shaw Communications Canada Inc., 2023 FCA 237 at para. 50
citations.why: Reasonableness standard applies to Board decision

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board's finding that the respondent did not sexually harass is unreasonable for two reasons.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board made contradictory findings on whether the respondent's conduct was sexual, rendering the decision unreasonable.

citations.cite: Canada (Minister of Citizenship and Immigration) v. Vavilov, 2019 SCC 65, [2019] 4 S.C.R. 653 at paras. 102–104
citations.why: Contradictory findings render decision unreasonable

citations.cite: Nowlan v. Canada (Attorney General), 2022 FCA 83 at paras. 27, 38
citations.why: Contradictory findings render decision unreasonable

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board's conclusion contradicts established case law that the respondent's repeated sexual comments constitute sexual harassment.

citations.cite: Vavilov at para. 112
citations.why: Failure to follow case law renders decision unreasonable

citations.cite: Canada (Attorney General) v. Poupart, 2022 FCA 77 at para. 49
citations.why: Failure to follow case law renders decision unreasonable

citations.cite: Entertainment Software Association v. Society of Composers, Authors and Music Publishers of Canada, 2020 FCA 100 at para. 33
citations.why: Failure to follow case law renders decision unreasonable

citations.cite: Bahniuk v. Canada (Attorney General), 2016 FCA 127 at para. 15
citations.why: Failure to follow case law renders decision unreasonable

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Decision must be set aside because the respondent's comments meet the definition of sexual harassment.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: No other grounds raised by WestJet justify intervention.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board considered the Policies, seriousness, and remorse; these aggravating factors must be re-weighed on remand.

citations.cite: David Harris, Wrongful Dismissal, 8th ed (Toronto: Thomson Reuters, 2025) [Harris] at § 5:60
citations.why: Aggravating factors justify more severe discipline

citations.cite: Brown & Beatty at § 7:33
citations.why: Aggravating factors justify more severe discipline

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The Board did not err in declining to make a credibility determination as differences were immaterial.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court finds no error in the Board's conclusion that the respondent had mental health challenges based on his testimony, rejecting the applicant's claim of no evidence.

summaries.speaker: court
summaries.summary: The court explains its discretion to remit cases for reconsideration per Vavilov and notes dismissal is not automatic in sexual harassment cases, so the Board must redetermine the complaint.
